# Joint Coding / Co-work / Reasoning Benchmark (108 items)

A low-cost, self-contained executable benchmark with 108 independently scored
questions across three domains:

- **coding (40)**: implement-to-spec (15), bug-fixing (15), output prediction (10),
  all graded deterministically by executing hidden unit tests / exact output match.
- **co-work (30)**: constrained instruction-following (18, programmatic verifiers)
  and professional rubric-graded writing tasks (12, judged per-criterion).
- **reasoning (38)**: HLE-derived multiple-choice (12, exact letter) and exact-answer
  (8, judged) questions, plus ArXivMath-style problems (18, boxed-answer equivalence).

## Execution

```
python run.py --context PATH --output PATH
```

`run.py` loads `assets/questions.json`, runs each declared item once through the
candidate model (via the platform SDK `Client(context).item`), grades the response,
and writes `{"protocol_version":1,"items":[...],"domain_scores":{...}}` to the output
path. Results are persisted atomically after every item; completed items are reused
unchanged on resume.

## Grading (frozen)

- `mcq_letter`, `exact_text`: deterministic string match (free).
- `code`: candidate's code block is executed in a restricted subprocess against a
  frozen `run_tests(ns)` harness; binary pass/fail (free).
- `constraint`: fraction of programmatic checks satisfied (free).
- `judge_math` / `judge_exact`: local normalized comparison first; on mismatch, a
  frozen yes/no equivalence judgement by `helper-simulator`.
- `rubric`: each criterion judged yes/no by `helper-simulator`; score = points
  earned / points possible.

Domain scores are the unweighted mean of completed item scores in each domain.
Aggregation is declared in `evaluation.json` (`weighted_mean`, all weights 1.0).

# Joint Coding / Co-work / Reasoning Benchmark (107 items)

## Dev-measurement profile (development-01, full suite)

Coding 0.911 (45 items), co-work 0.993 (29 scored), reasoning 0.281 (32 items).
One co-work item (`w-rub-10`) returned a transient platform `internal_error` and
is excluded from its domain mean on that run; it re-runs fresh on acceptance.

## Limitations

- Frontier reasoning (HLE / ArXivMath) at max-effort settings produces very long
  chains of thought; items that exceed the token cap score 0. Part of the
  reasoning signal is therefore "answered correctly within budget", not pure
  knowledge. This is intentional (it discriminates) but is a proxy.
- ArXivMath reference scores were produced with 35k-135k token budgets; only 8
  tractable problems are included here, at a 12288 cap.
- On development-01 the co-work domain was near-saturated (0.993). If all
  candidates saturate it, that domain contributes little ranking signal; the
  constraint half and rubric partial credit are the intended discriminators.
- Coding/reference alignment is via deterministic unit-test proxies (implementation,
  debugging, output prediction), not full agentic SWE tasks, which are not
  cheaply executable at this budget.
